title: You Thought It Was Just Love… Until You Realized God Was In It
paragraphs:
You Thought It Was Just Love… Until You Realized God Was In It
The Quiet, Unmistakable Signs You’re Dating Someone Who Carries Heaven in Their Heart
You didn’t notice it at first.
It didn’t come with fireworks or a dramatic voice from heaven. No thunder. No flashing signs. Just… peace. Strange, unfamiliar peace in places where your past relationships felt like war zones.
And maybe that’s what confused you.

Because you were used to chaos. Used to guessing. Used to wondering where you stood. Used to loving harder than you were loved. Used to carrying conversations, carrying emotions, carrying the weight of something that was never equally held.
But this time… something is different.
Not perfect. Not flawless. But different in a way that feels… sacred.

You started noticing the way they speak—not just to you, but about people who aren’t in the room. No gossip. No tearing others down to feel bigger. Just quiet restraint. A heart that seems governed by something deeper.

Because Scripture whispers this truth in the original Greek:
“ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ” (ek gar tou perisseumatos tēs kardias to stoma lalei) — “For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.” (Matthew 12:34)
And suddenly, you realize… their words feel clean because their heart is being cleansed.
You start noticing how they handle conflict.
Not with manipulation. Not with silent punishment. Not with explosive anger that leaves emotional scars. But with a willingness to understand. To pause. To choose humility over being right.
And it catches you off guard.
Because the world taught you that power in relationships comes from control.

But they live like they believe something else entirely:
“בְּרַךְ־לֵבָב יִקָּרֵא נָבוֹן” (berakh-levav yiqqare navon) — “The pure in heart is called discerning.” (Proverbs 22:11, Hebrew context)
They don’t just react… they discern.

And maybe for the first time, you feel safe enough to be honest. Not the curated version of you. Not the strong version. The real version. The one still healing. The one still wrestling. The one that still has questions you’re afraid to say out loud.
And they don’t run.
They don’t shrink back when they see your scars.
Instead, they gently remind you—sometimes without even quoting Scripture—that healing is possible.
Because they live it.
You notice how they talk about God.
Not like a performance. Not like a script. Not like something they use to impress people. But like someone they actually know.
Like He’s real to them.
Like He’s present in their decisions, their fears, their hopes.
“καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν” (kai esontai hoi duo eis sarka mian) — “And the two shall become one flesh.” (Ephesians 5:31)
But they understand something deeper than romance.
They know oneness isn’t just physical… it’s spiritual alignment.
And here’s where it starts to hit you…
You’re not just dating someone who likes you.
You’re walking alongside someone who fears God.
“יִרְאַת יְהוָה רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה” (Yir’at Adonai reshit chokhmah) — “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.” (Proverbs 9:10)
And that changes everything.
Because someone who truly fears God won’t play with your heart casually.
They understand accountability. They understand that love is not just a feeling—it’s a responsibility before heaven.
You see it in their boundaries.
Not restrictions meant to control you… but guardrails meant to protect what God is building.
They don’t rush you into sin.
They don’t pressure you into compromise.
They don’t make you feel guilty for wanting to honour God.
Instead… they make obedience feel possible.
And that’s when something inside you breaks open.
Because you realize… this isn’t just about them.
This is about you, too.
About how God is using them to reveal the areas in your life that still need surrender.
Because godly love doesn’t just comfort—it convicts.
It doesn’t just affirm—it refines.
“ἁγιάζω” (hagiazō) — to sanctify, to set apart, to make holy.
That’s what this kind of relationship does.
It pulls you closer to Jesus… not away from Him.
Be honest.
Have you ever been in something that made you pray less?
That made you compromise more?
That made you feel distant from God?
And now… this feels different.
Now you feel drawn back.

Back to Scripture.
Back to prayer.
Back to repentance.
Back to Jesus.
And maybe that’s the clearest sign of all.
Because a godly relationship doesn’t replace God.
It reveals Him.
It magnifies Him.
It points you back to the One who wrote your story before you even understood your own heart.
And here’s the truth most people don’t say out loud…
Godly doesn’t mean perfect.
It means surrendered.
It means when they fall, they repent.
When they’re wrong, they admit it.
When they struggle, they don’t hide it.
Because they understand grace.
They live under it.
They depend on it.
“χάρις” (charis) — grace. Undeserved favour. Divine empowerment.
And maybe that’s why this relationship feels so different…
Because it’s not built on performance.
It’s built on grace.
So if you’re reading this and something deep inside you is stirring… don’t ignore it.
This might not just be emotions.
This might be confirmation.
And if you’ve been questioning whether what you have is from God…
Look at the fruit.
Look at the direction.
Look at what it’s doing to your soul.

Because Jesus said:
“By their fruits you will know them.” (Matthew 7:16)
Not by their words.
Not by their charm.
By their fruit.
So ask yourself honestly…
Is this relationship bringing me closer to Christ… or pulling me away?
And if the answer is closer…
Protect it.
Pray over it.
Don’t take it lightly.
Because what God is building… the enemy will try to destroy.
And this is where you come in.
Someone you love needs to read this.
And be honest…
Don’t stay silent. Your voice matters here.
Because we don’t just talk about love—we walk people through transformation, through Scripture, through real-life struggles, through healing that actually lasts.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper in Christ…
Because this isn’t just content.
This is your soul.
This is your eternity.
And maybe… just maybe…
God didn’t just bring that person into your life to love you.
He brought them to lead you back to Him.
And that changes everything.
